subject: RE: GDPR Data Subject Request — access & deletion scoping
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finpay.eu>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: DPO Team <dpo@finpay.eu>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: GDPR Data Subject Request — access & deletion scoping

Hi Vivek,

We received a DSR from one of our EU users asking for (1) a full export of their account data and model interaction transcripts and (2) permanent deletion of all data you process on our behalf. Before we respond to the user, our legal team needs two things from Redwood: a short scoping document that explains what Redwood can export vs what remains with FinPay, and an operational timeline for producing exports and confirming deletion when requested.

We also need clarification on controller/processor responsibilities in the following scenarios:
- Hosted API requests (customer data passed through Redwood API to models)
- Logs/audit records retained for troubleshooting/security
- Backups and cached KV entries used for inference

Can you confirm whether Redwood will provide:
- a sample export format (CSV/JSON) for transcripts and metadata,
- a deletion confirmation template for our records, and
- estimated turnaround (in business days) for both export and deletion artifacts.

We are under a tight SLA to respond to the data subject within 30 days, so any detail you can provide in the next 48 hours would be very helpful.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
DPO, FinPay Inc.

--
Attachment: none
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finpay.eu>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: RE: GDPR Data Subject Request — access & deletion scoping

Elena — thanks for flagging this. Looping in Neha (privacy lead) and Karthik (security/compliance) who can provide the technical/export details.

Proposed next steps from our side:
1) Neha will attach a short DSR playbook describing what Redwood can export and the format we typically deliver.
2) Karthik will confirm logs and retention windows and provide a sample log export (sanitized).
3) We will provide a deletion confirmation template you can keep for your records.

We can commit to an initial package (playbook + sample export + template) within 3 business days if we have the request scope. If you expect multiple accounts or historical bulk requests, please indicate quantity and date ranges — that may take longer.

Also: Quick question for you — does FinPay want us to process deletion requests only after you issue a controller instruction (preferred), or should Redwood accept DSRs directly from end users in this engagement?

Best,
Vivek
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: DPA_DSR_Process.pdf (attached)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finpay.eu>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:24:00 +0000
Subject: RE: GDPR Data Subject Request — access & deletion scoping

Hi Elena —

Thanks — I attached our short DSR playbook (DPA_DSR_Process.pdf) which covers:
- What Redwood stores when acting as a processor (request payloads, temporary KV cache, model outputs)
- What remains with the controller (customer account, billing, and any off-platform archives you manage)
- Standard export formats: transcripts -> JSONL per-session, metadata -> CSV (see sample attached)
- Typical timelines and SLAs when we act on instructions from the controller

Key clarifications up front:
- Role: Redwood is a processor for model interactions and derived outputs when acting on FinPay traffic via the hosted API. We process strictly per your instructions in the DPA.
- Exports: We can provide session transcripts and API request/response metadata. We do NOT retain third-party model provider logs beyond the ranges in our retention policy; if you have downstream model provider logs, those are separate.
- Deletion: We will permanently delete data we control on receipt of a valid controller instruction. We can provide a signed deletion confirmation when deletion completes.

Operational timelines (typical):
- Small scoped DSR (single user, <30 sessions): export in 3 business days; deletion in 5 business days from receipt of controller instruction.
- Large or historical requests (bulk ranges, >10k sessions): export 7–15 business days; deletion timelines may require a scheduled maintenance window.

Attached: log_export_sample.csv (sanitized), and the DPA_DSR_Process.pdf playbook. I’ve also included a short deletion confirmation template below you can use; we will sign and return after completion.

-- Deletion confirmation template (excerpt) --
Redwood Inference confirms that on <date> the data elements listed below for subject <identifier> were permanently deleted from Redwood-controlled systems.
Elements deleted:
- API request payloads (timestamps, session ids),
- Model outputs and inference caches associated with the session ids above,
- Temporary KV cache entries generated during inference.

Signed,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

Best,
Neha

--
Attachments: log_export_sample.csv, DPA_DSR_Process.pdf
From: Samir Patel <samir@finpay.eu>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finpay.eu>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 15:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: GDPR Data Subject Request — access & deletion scoping

Thanks Neha — that helps. A couple of follow ups:

1) Can you confirm the retention windows for audit logs vs. session transcripts? Our GDPR policy requires us to document retention for the user.
2) We need the signed SCCs and the exact clause reference in the DPA that binds Redwood to act only on controller instructions for deletion. Can you attach a redlined pointer or clause snippet?

If possible please attach the SCCs and a sample signed deletion confirmation we can import into our ticket for the user.

Samir
General Counsel, FinPay Inc.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finpay.eu>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 17:02:00 +0000
Subject: RE: GDPR Data Subject Request — access & deletion scoping

Samir / Elena — attaching the signed SCCs and a deletion confirmation template you can use (dsr_deletion_confirmation_template.txt).

Retention clarification (short):
- Session transcripts / API request metadata: retained 90 days by default. Can be configured per contract; longer retention requires contract amendment.
- Audit logs / security telemetry: retained 1 year by default (used for incident response). Copies used for compliance evidence are archived for up to 2 years per our archival policy.

Clause pointer: Section 3.1 (Processing and Instructions) of our DPA states Redwood acts only on controller instructions for processing and deletion. I copied the exact clause into the attached PDF for your convenience (SCCs_signed.pdf contains the SCCs and DPA clause excerpt).

Next steps:
- We’ll sign and return a deletion confirmation within 48 hours of receiving FinPay’s controller instruction that identifies the subject and scope.
- If you want Redwood to accept DSRs directly from end users (instead of only controller instructions), we need a short amendment to the DPA and an operational routing process; happy to scope that if required.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: SCCs_signed.pdf, dsr_deletion_confirmation_template.txt
